paper_metadata.title: Achieving high strength and ductility in a dual-phase Mg-Li alloy via rotary swaging

evidence.quote: Achieving both high strength and ductility remains a challenge in dual-phase Mg-Li alloys. Although the high strength has been achieved through heat treatment or conventional deformation techniques, these methods result in low ductility. The Mg-8Li-3Zn-0.5Y alloy was processed using low-strain room-temperature rotary swaging (RS)

the blocky α-Mg phases are uniformly dispersed within the β-Li matrix in the as-cast alloy, with an average thickness of approximately 20 μm

attributes.location: near phase boundary and within β-Li matrix

Results indicated that the identified phases include α-Mg, β-Li, Mg3Zn3Y2, Mg24Y5 and Mg2Zn11 phases.
an average grain size of α-Mg phases is ~ 6.54 μm and an average grain size of β-Li phases is ~ 4.80 μm.
the recrystallized grains account for 50.53 % and β-Li phases are refined via dynamic recrystallization
massive finer secondary particles (~ 1 μm) are distributed along the ED within the β-Li matrix in the as-extruded alloy. Both Zn and Y are enriched in these secondary particles.
subsequent RS further refined α-Mg band widths and reduced the grain size of β-Li phase along the feed direction (FD)
good ductility is attributed to β -Li phases with fine dynamically recrystallized grains aligned along the extrusion direction (ED)

attributes.composition: Zn/Y atomic ratio at point A = 1.87

A high brightness in EDS mappings indicates that Zn segregation occurs at the grain boundary of the β-Li phase, while Y exhibits no apparent segregation
Grain refinement constitutes the primary strengthening mechanism.
Those precipitates mainly play the role of precipitation strengthening in the Mg-Li-Zn-Y alloys.
numerous MgLi2Zn nano-precipitates and massive accumulated dislocations
Twinning-mediated lattice reorientation transforms initially unfavorable slip orientations into favorably aligned configurations, facilitating further plastic flow.

amplified lattice friction against dislocation motion elevates deformation resistance. Therefore, the strength of the swaged alloy is improved and the ductility is reduced.
